verdicts.reason: Night desk, key-lit pool, a low-poly user at a window-framed laptop and a slow push-in with a clear focal subject. Caption sits top, out of the way. The amber ball is already on the floor. B-01 was judged mostly from the strips. Weakness: the background slab skyline is nearly black.
The camera follows the amber pulse along the floor conduit toward rdp01 with parallax and depth of field. The pulse leads the camera. Host plates are a bit UI-like but readable.
A dolly arrives at the server with the listener lighting on its front. The server has a key light and rim, a floor pool and parallax from the CA vaults and AD. Caption does not cover the server.

The pale self-signed card appears at the listener, then is carried to the client side. 'Unverified' and 'Self-signed' sit on separate plates and the amber channel dies to grey. It is cinematic motion, but the focal card shrinks to about 40 px in b and c (finding CIN-S1R2-01).

A real camera swing follows the template badge as it drops from the AD pillar onto the server, with changing lens and depth. The badge is a white pill that is close in colour and shape to a request capsule (finding CIN-S1R2-13).
The server door swings open and the camera pushes into the chassis. The private key (ring key) and public key (small hex) form with entrance motion, not opacity only.

The key drops onto the safe lid, is swallowed and the safe closes with a lock dial. Heavy shadow grain and a very dark c frame, and the public hex is cropped at the top edge. Composition is clumsy but it is a real shot.
The hex joins the info tile in a glass capsule while the safe stays shut. Caption is bottom, off the subject. Silhouettes are distinct.
The safe flares and emits a beam that seals the capsule, and a seal band appears on the capsule. The beam is a hard-edged white wedge that reads as a pointer rod (finding CIN-S1R2-14).

The camera pulls back from the safe to frame the server, AD and both CAs. A steel-blue diamond query pulse runs. The capsule hangs in front of AD's pillar base in b and c, which reads as heading to AD (finding CIN-S1R2-08).
The capsule travels the cyan lit route alone, the camera leads it into the CA1 vault, and the vault grows as the lens approaches. Strong parallax and depth.

Camera is inside the vault with staggered ticks. The four check plates run in a column over the press and across the capsule and module (c). The interior is a flat saturated teal wash with noisy shadows (findings CIN-S1R2-02 and CIN-S1R2-07).

The press stamps the card and the camera drifts out with the card as focal subject. SAN and EKU plates are readable. The card is a plain slab with no validity bar or AIA/CDP ports (finding CIN-S1R2-12).
The card follows the lit route back to the server and docks beside the safe, with an orbiting camera and a layered background.

A real crane up to the gold vault on its plinth, with a cable-free base and a ring seal revealed by a light sweep. The key module is dark. The 'Root CA' plate is stippled in c as it fades (finding CIN-S1R2-15).

The motivated cut into a desaturated flashback with cream ceremony lighting is clear. The CA request and the 'Earlier' tag read in the strip, but the cyan CA=true band is not identifiable in the desaturated frames (finding CIN-S1R2-11). Tags in c are ghosted and speckled on the vault.

The cut back to the present continues into a pull-back and orbit. Trust arcs grow from the CA crowns to the root and the camera reveals the whole lab. The arc is thin and reads pale cream-white, with the gold end weak.

A continuous swoop from the wide shot to the client, with a new amber channel. The declared focal subject CERT-RDP is a few pixels across and the key pulse and handshake proof are not visible in any frame or tile (finding CIN-S1R2-06).

The cards dock upward into a stack with the gold trust-store cradle. Labels are stacked on plates. The camera moves, but it is the closest this film gets to a slide, with a vertical card stack and label plates.
A close push-in with depth of field. AIA tags sit to one side of the chain. The AIA indicator is an unexplained plain hexagon near the chair.

Six tilted label plates in a checklist column sit across or beside a flat vertical card stack, with 'Θ'-looking tick rings detached from their text. Labels vary in size and cross the focal chain in b. The tiles read as a checklist overlay, not a filmed action.

In a the seven-plate list fills the centre and covers the whole chain. The declared focal CDP kiosk sits at the frame edge, small. The amber pellets (the CRL fetches) are tiny. It is a text list with a hint of scene behind it.
The channel turns green and the camera tracks along it. The caption appears with the green channel. The session window is only a small pale slab at the desk. In c the cards are edge-on slivers.
A glide along the green channel to WEB01 with a pivot and parallax. A WEB01 plate overprints the fading CA1 label in b, and rdp01 appears twice.
Door opens, key pair forms, key locks in the safe and the capsule is sealed by a beam. It matches the RDP beat language, with depth and caption below.

The camera rises over AD. CA1 dims to pale grey and CA2 lights violet, and the plates sit apart. A thin vertical grey rod runs from the web server badge up to the CA2 label. It is a static straight connector (finding CIN-S1R2-05).
The capsule runs only along the violet route into CA2, and the camera leads it. Fading plates show hashed alpha in a (see CIN-S1R2-15). The grey rod persists.
The camera is inside the violet vault with the same check language as S4 and staggered ticks. The capsule is partly hidden behind the plates in b and c. The compressed pace is clear.
The press stamps the TLS certificate and it is carried back. In c a server door and a wide white badge slab sit very near the lens and a tall grey rod crosses the frame (finding CIN-S1R2-04).

A lateral move reveals the CA2 trust link and the camera pulls out. In a a near-lens black vertical bar spans the frame and a white slab fills the bottom. A finite floor edge with a corner is visible in c.
A flat chain stack faces the camera beside a four-plate checklist (b, c). The amber route has hard polyline corners. It repeats the S6 slide-like layout, compressed, with little camera motivation.

A rising orbit shows the gold root over cyan and violet arcs. Servers and the user are cropped out of the bottom of the frame. The bottom-edge labels crowd and overlap and the arcs are thin (finding CIN-S1R2-03).
The title settles over the scene and the world fades to a clean black end, with no pops. The title plate sits across the root and CA1 focal area in a (finding CIN-S1R2-10).

findings.evidence: The declared focal subjects are tiny. The self-signed card is about 40 px wide in a wide shot of the whole lab. In B-06.1 the CERT-RDP cards are a few pixels at the far end of a wide pull. In B-06.5 the pki kiosk is at the frame edge and the two amber CRL fetches are a handful of pixels beside a seven-plate list. The shots shown are close to those flagged in CIN-S1R1-06.
findings.why: A viewer cannot identify the subject that carries the beat; there is no clear focal subject.
findings.direction: Frame each of these beats so the declared focal subject is a clear share of the frame at its hold. Move the camera in at the moment the card, cards-with-proof or CRL fetch is the event, instead of showing it in a wide.

findings.evidence: In B-06.5_a the stack of check plates covers the chain cards (the first plate sits over the gold root card). In B-06.4_b the plates are different sizes and tilts and overlap the chair and desk. In B-04.3_c and B-08.1_c, plates cover the press and capsule (the 'Enroll permission granted' plate sits on the capsule). Ticks in B-06.4_c are separated from their text.
findings.why: Check lists must stand beside the focal subject at one size, facing camera, not across the chain or capsule. This repeats CIN-S1R1-04, LEG-S1R1-04 and LEG-S1R1-06.
findings.direction: Place check lists beside the subject on one camera-facing plane at one size, clear of the chain, capsule and press. Keep each tick next to its text.

findings.evidence: Behind the action there is a flat ground plane that ends at a visible edge and corner against a pure black void (top right of B-08.3_c and B-09.2_c; B-09.1 a). The dark slab skyline in S6 and S7 stops at a hard horizon with black above. The hero B-09.2_c crops the RDP server, web server and user out of frame at the bottom edge.
findings.why: CIN-S1R1-13 asked for a background layer with no finite floor edge, and the hero shot has to show the complete topology including the user consuming both services. The edge and void flatten the wide shots and the cropped hero shows less than half of the topology.
findings.direction: Extend and fade the ground and give the horizon a continuous background layer (mist wall, distant lights or gradient). Re-compose B-09.2 so root, both CAs, both servers and the user fit with margin.

findings.evidence: In B-08.2_c the web server's open door fills the left of the frame and a wide white badge slab sits across the top. In B-08.3_a a vertical black bar spans the whole frame height near the lens and a white slab fills the bottom edge. The dark rod and slab belong to the web server badge and rod.
findings.why: Per CIN-S1R1-10 camera moves must not enter label space or clip geometry. A near-lens bar across the frame reads as a glitch or tracking error.
findings.direction: Keep the camera path clear of the web server badge, the rod and the server door. Offset the move or hide the rod while the camera passes.

findings.evidence: A thin straight grey vertical rod runs from the template badge on each server up to the CA label or vault (a long rod from the web badge to the 'Issuing CA 2' label in B-07.4_b, one above rdp01 in B-05.1_a and B-07.4_a). It stays static and straight between nodes.
findings.why: Criteria C-01 allows no static straight connectors drawn between nodes; every line-like object must be a channel or trust link that grows or flows. The rod is neither, and reads as connector grammar.
findings.direction: If the rod is the AD lookup, make it the steel-blue query pulse that travels to AD and back. If it is a badge stem, shorten it so it is not near any CA. If it is neither, remove it.

findings.evidence: No frame or strip tile shows the key pulse inside the closed container, the handshake proof (signature impression) travelling, arriving at the client or dissolving. At the client the only moving elements are cards. The only unexplained shape in S6 is a plain white hexagon beside the chair in B-06.3_b and B-06.3_c.
findings.why: PKI-S1R1-06 required the pulse, the proof's arrival and its verification to be readable at film scale. They are not, so proof of possession (F-10) is not shown.
findings.direction: Give B-06.1 a close composition for the container pulse, the proof leaving the server and being matched at the client, with the proof's own silhouette, and name the hexagon in B-06.3 or remove it.

findings.evidence: The CA vault interiors are lit as a uniformly bright saturated teal or violet field with pools of black, noisy shadow under the press and capsule; the safe interior in B-03.2 is a grey wash with heavy grain and B-03.2_c is almost black.
findings.why: CIN-S1R1-12 asked for a visible key and rim on the focal subject and less emissive wash. The focal subject sits in the middle of ambient colour and shadow noise, so lit-side to shadow-side contrast cannot read.
findings.direction: Reduce the emissive and ambient fill, light the focal object with a key and rim, and increase shadow sample quality or soften the light to remove noise.

findings.evidence: The capsule hangs about 100 px from the server, level with the base of the AD pillar and overlapping its silhouette from the camera angle. A steel-blue diamond sits beside it. The capsule is not at the server's own outbound port.
findings.why: PKI-S1R1-02 requires the capsule to be held at the server's own port, clearly apart from AD, with the query pulse as the event. As framed it can read as sent to AD.
findings.direction: Hold the capsule at the server's port on the near side, with the camera angle placing a clear gap between it and AD. Keep the query pulse as the only thing that travels to AD.

findings.evidence: In B-07.1_b the WEB01 and portal plates overprint the fading '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label, and 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab' appears twice in one frame. In B-09.2_c the WEB01 plate is partly covered by the portal plate.
findings.why: LEG-S1R1-08: host, site and CA plates must not overlap.
findings.direction: Re-space or time the plates so that none overlap, and fade the outgoing label before the incoming one arrives.

findings.evidence: The title plate runs across the middle of the frame over the root vault base, the CA1 vault and the trust arcs. The focal subject ROOT_CA is directly above and touching.
findings.why: The caption must not cover the focal action.
findings.direction: Fade the world's labels first and move the camera so the root sits above the title, or place the title in the free lower third.

findings.evidence: The capsule is a small grey-white shape in the strip and the cyan CA=true band is not readable in the desaturated frames. The sealing by Issuing CA 1's module is not visible in a, b or c.
findings.why: PKI-S1R1-10: the CA request needs a visible band and a visible sealing.
findings.direction: Keep one saturated cyan accent (the CA=true band) in the flashback, and show the module sealing the request in a clear frame.

findings.evidence: The issued card is a plain pale slab. No validity bar or small AIA/CDP ports are visible in any frame.
findings.why: PKI-S1R1-08 asked for a validity bar and ports on the issued card.
findings.direction: Add a visible validity bar and two small ports to the issued card geometry and light them in the press beat.

findings.evidence: The RDPAuth template badge is a flat white pill sitting on top of the server in every later beat. It is the same bright neutral white as a request capsule and nearly the same stadium silhouette from above.
findings.why: Request white is reserved for requests, and a pill that stays on the server can be taken for a request.
findings.direction: Give the badge its own colour and a flatter plate silhouette distinct from the capsule.

findings.evidence: The proof-of-possession beam is a hard-edged, opaque white wedge between the safe and the capsule, with no glow or falloff.
findings.why: CIN-S1R1-16 asked for a soft tapering light, not a rod.
findings.direction: Make the beam additive, soft-edged and fading toward the capsule, and remove the opaque white edge.

findings.evidence: Plates fading in or out show hashed alpha (stipple). '1SN0S Root CA' in B-05.1_c, the tags in B-05.2_c and the 1SN0S.LAB and eligibility plates in B-07.4_a have a speckled texture.
findings.why: CIN-S1R1-05 required no speckle on captions or plates.
findings.direction: Fade plates with true alpha blend (or scale and fade together), never hashed or dithered transparency.

findings.evidence: The validation ticks are rings with a bar inside, which read as 'Θ' or a power icon. The check rings in the CA vaults read as a 'G' glyph.
findings.why: The tick is a shape in the vocabulary and has to read as a tick.
findings.direction: Use a recognisable tick mark, or a ring that completes with a visible tick, keeping the shape distinct in greyscale.

findings.evidence: The session window is a small pale rectangle at the desk and is not identifiable. The green channel and caption land together but nothing opens.
findings.why: B-06.6 says the channel turns green and the session window opens.
findings.direction: Show the session window opening with an entrance (scale and light) that is readable at the end of the move.

findings.evidence: The issuer arcs are thin and read cream or white with very little gold, only blending to cyan or lilac at the CA ends. Dense label plates sit around them.
findings.why: PKI-S1R1-05 asked for gold at the root blending into the CA colour and never a white wire.
findings.direction: Thicken the arc and saturate the gold end so it is clearly gold at the root, reading as light and not a wire.
